Adding one to a story that doesn't, as one deleted while a proposal naming it waited, or by another window, or whose file was removed from `.suspense/planning/` meanwhile, changes nothing: no story is made for it, no other story is given it, and nothing is saved. It says so in plain words where it was asked for, as "That story no longer exists, so the step wasn't added", in the theme's error colour, as the states say, with what was to be added kept, so it can be added to another story or as a new one. A step added to a story already sent is refused the same way, saying the story has been sent.

## Layout

Everything in Planning is laid out on one rhythm, so it scans as a single list. The column has 24 pixels of padding at its top and sides. Each section's heading is a row 32 pixels tall: its name in small semibold text, its count beside it, muted, and its actions at its right, each a labelled button, never an icon alone; 8 pixels beneath it its first row. Story rows are 36 pixels tall, 2 pixels apart, each with 12 pixels of padding at either side, their parts in fixed columns, so the grips, mode pills, titles, and statuses line up down the whole list: the grip 16 pixels, the mode pill 72 pixels, the title the rest, the status and time right-aligned in a column of their own 96 pixels wide, then the row's buttons. Sections are 24 pixels apart. Every row's state reads the same way, as below, and every label is the same small text, muted where it is secondary.
From top to bottom, Planning reads: the pause bar, while paused; Current sprint, while a sprint is under way; Next sprint; Backlog; Findings; and Done, collapsed. Each is a section headed as above, so nothing sits outside the rhythm, and an open story, a drafting or research panel, and the citations and steps inside a story all use the same three parts, below.

## Parts

Everything in Planning is built from three parts, each always drawn the same way:
- A row: 36 pixels tall, in the fixed columns above, for stories, steps, findings, and Done; its secondary text muted and cut off with an ellipsis, its buttons small ghost buttons with labels, shown at its right on hover and always while it is focused
- A panel: an inset area 16 pixels below what opened it, on the theme's raised surface, corners rounded 6 pixels, 12 pixels of padding, a heading row of 32 pixels with its name, as "Draft stories", "Research", or the story's title, and its close button, its content beneath, and its actions in a footer row, right-aligned, the primary action last; used for an open story, drafting, and research
- A card: a box inside a panel, on the theme's base surface, with a 1 pixel line in the theme's line colour, corners rounded 4 pixels, 12 pixels of padding, 8 pixels from the next; a label row at its top, its content, and a footer row of labelled buttons; used for proposals and for each finding's summary
Labels are words, never icons alone: every button reads what it does, "Accept", "Send sprint", "Start automatically", and an icon beside a label only repeats it. Each heading's count is a plain number, muted, and each status a coloured label, as the states say. The pause bar is a row across the column's top, 40 pixels tall, its text and buttons on one line, the same height whatever it says.

## States

Each part of Planning has the same few states, shown the same way wherever they come up, so a state is never guessed from what is missing.
- Empty: a single muted line, centred in the section, saying what is missing and what to do, as "Nothing planned. Drag stories here, or press Ctrl+N.", with no illustration
- Loading: a spinner and a short muted label of what is happening, as "Drafting stories…", in the place the result will appear, never a blank space
- Paused: a story whose task is paused shows "Paused" as its status, in the theme's warning colour, with a small pause icon, and a "Resume" button in its row, as the PromptSending says of pausing; a sprint with any story paused says so in its heading, as "1 paused", in the same colour
- Error: a line in the theme's error colour, saying what went wrong in plain words, with what the harness or the application reported beneath it collapsed under "Details", and a "Try again" button where trying again can help
A story's status in its row is the same coloured label a task has, as the [MessageList](../prompt-mode/message-list/index.md#message-list)'s status says, Queued, Running with its spinner and time, Done, Failed, Cancelled, Paused, or, where its task can't be found, Task missing, as the sprint says, and a story not yet sent shows nothing there, so its absence means "not sent".
Each part shows each state that can come up for it, worded for it:
- Story list: empty, "Nothing planned. Press Ctrl+N to add a story." in Next sprint and "Nothing waiting." in the Backlog; loading, while the plan is read on opening, a row of skeleton rows, never an empty section; error, when the plan can't be read or saved, saying which file and why, with "Try again"
- Research and its findings: loading, the live line of what it is reading with its spinner; empty, "No findings yet." in Findings; error, the run's failure with "Try again", which keeps the question in its box; a finding that ended early, as stopped, marked "Incomplete", muted, in its row
- Pause: the pause bar, in the theme's warning colour, as the paused section says, and the sprint's Send buttons disabled with their tooltips saying why; a sprint that can't start for a failed story says so in its heading, in the same colour
- Proposals: loading, the drafting line and spinner; empty, "No stories proposed." with "Draft again"; error, the run's failure with "Try again"; a proposal with no spec cited, in the warning colour with "Draft again", as the spec grounding says

## Drafting

Drafting stories shows its work in one place, a panel opened beneath the Backlog's heading, never in a popup that hides the list. It has the request box at its top, labelled "Describe what you want", and beneath it, while the run goes, its research: a muted line of what the harness is doing, as "Reading the spec…", with its spinner, updating as it goes, and a "Stop" button. Once it ends, the panel lists its proposals, as below, then "Accept all" and "Reject all" buttons along the panel's foot, and closes itself once none is left to decide. A run that fails shows its error, as the states say, and leaves the request in its box to try again; one that proposes nothing says so, as an empty state. Proposals are kept until each is decided, so closing Planning and coming back finds them as they were.
Drafting can also be started from an open story, with "Ask agent" in its row's menu or the open story's footer: the request box then reads "What does this story need?", the run is told the story's title and prompt, and the panel opens beneath that story rather than the Backlog's heading.
The request is sent with the panel's "Draft" button, its primary action, or by pressing Enter in the request box, whichever label it reads; Ctrl+Enter there starts it too, and the button's tooltip gives Enter as its shortcut. Shift+Enter adds a new line in the box and sends nothing. A request that is empty, or only spaces and new lines, starts nothing, and the button is disabled while it is. While a run is going, Enter starts no second one, and the button is disabled. Enter in the request box only ever sends the request: the list's Enter, opening or closing the focused story, never fires while focus is in the box.

## Proposals

The agent never writes the plan itself. Its run is a Question run, as the [Sandbox](../sandbox/index.md#sandbox) says, able to read the project and change nothing, and Suspense data is never granted to it, so it can't touch `.suspense/planning/`; it only proposes, and nothing it proposes reaches the plan until the user accepts it.
Each proposal is one concrete task, with a title, a prompt, and the mode that fits it, and says where it should go: either "New story", to become a story of its own, or "Add to" a story, naming an existing story the run was shown, the open story first, to be added to it. The planning prompt of the [BakedSystemPrompts](../harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts) asks for each proposal as a fenced block whose info string is `suspense-story`, holding its title, its mode, its target, `new` or the story's id, its `spec` list of citations into the Piton source, as the spec grounding says, and its prompt, so the application reads it whatever else the reply says. The planning prompt explains the form with an example, as:
```suspense-story
title: Close a finished sprint
mode: chain
target: new
spec:
- spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.sprint: when Close sprint shows
- No match: archiving a closed sprint
prompt:
Close sprint is offered once every story of the current sprint has
ended, as spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.sprint says.
```
A block that names a story that no longer exists is shown as "New story", with a muted note saying so.

## Spec Grounding

A drafted story is grounded in the project's spec, never written from the request alone. Before proposing, the drafter searches the spec for what each story touches: the requirements and behaviours it changes or relies on, the names it uses, as a feature, a component, or a property, and the sections they are in. It reads the spec as every run does, from its compiled reference or from what `piton slice` prints, never from the Piton source, as the [ModeSystemPrompts](../prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.md#mode-system-prompts) says, and the planning prompt of the [BakedSystemPrompts](../harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts) tells it to.
Each proposal cites what it found, specifically: its `suspense-story` block holds a `spec` list, one entry per element, each a link to the element in the spec's Piton source, under the spec location, never to the compiled reference: the .pi file, relative to the project directory, then `#` and the element it names, an anchor or a property on one, in the form `piton slice` takes, as `spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.sprint`, with a short line of what in it the story touches. The story's prompt names those elements and links to them in the same form. Only elements the drafter found are cited, and where they point is the only thing that is Piton source: the drafter still learns what the spec says only from the compiled reference or from what `piton slice` prints, never by reading the Piton source, as the [ModeSystemPrompts](../prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.md#mode-system-prompts) says, and works out each element's source from what `piton slice` prints for it, which names the file each declaration is in.
The application checks each link against the Piton source when the proposal arrives: the file has to exist under the spec location, and has to define the named element, the anchor declared in it and, for a property, that property on it, as `piton slice` would find it. A link that fails either check is dropped, with a muted note on the card saying which link it dropped and why, "no such file" or "the file doesn't define Planning.sprint". Each citation, on the proposal card and in an accepted story's "Spec" list, opens that place in the Piton source, the file in the editor at the element's declaration, as the [OpenFile](../open-file/index.md#open-file) opens a file.
Where no spec element matches part of a story, as a request for something the spec doesn't describe yet, the story says so instead of inventing one: its `spec` list holds an entry reading "No match", with what was looked for, and its prompt says plainly that the spec has nothing on it yet, so the change is new. A proposal with no element at all, and no "No match", isn't shown as a story: its card says the drafter cited no spec, in the theme's warning colour, with "Draft again", which runs the draft for that story once more.
The citations are shown on the proposal's card, beneath its prompt, as a short list, each element's name, as `Planning.sprint`, and its file, muted, as a link that opens that place in the Piton source, a "No match" entry muted with a small marker, and are kept with the story once it is accepted, listed in the open story beneath its steps as "Spec", and shown in its row's tooltip. They can be edited with the story, removed, or added to by hand: "Add citation" opens a picker of the spec's elements, its anchors and their properties, found from the Piton source and searched by name, never from the compiled reference, and adds the one picked in the same form, checked as a proposal's are.
Each citation says what kind of element it is, "Requirement", "Behaviour", "Name", or "Section", shown as a small muted label before it, and quotes the few words of the spec it rests on, so what the story relies on can be checked at a glance. Grounding holds for every proposal, however it came: from Draft stories, from research that ends with proposals, and from an Ask answer's `suspense-story` block, each checked and flagged the same way when it arrives.

## Proposal Cards

Each proposal is a card in the panel, in the order given: a label at its top, "New story" in the theme's accent, or, for an addition, "Add to this story" where it targets the story the research or draft was started from, and "Add to" and the story's title otherwise, in the story's own mode's colour, so where it will go is always read before anything else on the card; its title, its mode pill, and its prompt beneath, clipped at four lines with "Read more"; and three buttons along its foot, "Accept", "Edit", and "Reject", reachable by Tab and labelled for a screen reader. Edit opens the card's title, prompt, mode, and target in place, the target a menu of "New story" and each story, to be changed before it is accepted; editing doesn't accept it. Reject removes the card, with a short "Undo" in its place for a few seconds.
Accept records it in the plan straight away, saved as any change to the plan is: a new story goes into the Backlog, at its end, in its mode, marked "From agent" with a small sparkle beside its title until it is first opened, its spec citations kept with it, whether it was accepted on its own card or with "Accept all", and whether it came from drafting, research, or an Ask answer. Accepting never adds anything to Next sprint, so it never starts a sprint, however Start automatically is set; an accepted story reaches a sprint only once it is moved to Next sprint, as the sprint says; an addition is added to the named story as a new step at its end, as its steps say, its attachments with it, and the story is marked "Updated by agent" until it is next opened, the new step shown highlighted the first time it is; where the story no longer exists by then, the step isn't added, as the steps say, and the card stays, its target changed to "New story", to be accepted again. A story already sent can't be added to: its proposals offer only "New story". Each card, once decided, goes from the panel, and an accepted one leaves a one-line muted note in its place, "Added to Backlog" or "Added to <story>", with a link that opens the story where it is, in the Backlog or its section.
Ask answers can propose the same way: a `suspense-story` block in an answer is shown as a proposal card, with the same Accept, Edit, and Reject, its accepting recording it in the plan as above, so a story can come out of a conversation without anything written silently.

## Research

The agent can be asked to research a topic before anything is planned or built: "Research", a button beside "Draft stories" on the Backlog's heading, and "Research" in an open story's menu, open a box labelled "What should be looked into?". Research runs as a read-only investigation, a Question run, as the [Sandbox](../sandbox/index.md#sandbox) says, which can read the project and the web and change nothing, given the research prompt of the [BakedSystemPrompts](../harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts), which asks for findings, not changes: what was found, where, with links to the files and lines it read, what it is unsure of, and what it would suggest, and it may end with proposals, as the proposals say. Its run is shown in the drafting panel as drafting's is, its live line of what it is reading, a Stop button, and its spinner.
Its findings are a document of their own, "Research: <topic>", rendered as markdown with its links clickable, shown in a Findings list beneath the Backlog, newest first, each a row with its topic, when it ran, and its state, and opening in a body tab of its own to read whole. Findings started from a story are also listed in that story, beneath its steps. They are saved with the plan, in `.suspense/planning/research/`, a markdown file each, so they can be read again later, and can be deleted from their row's menu.

## Paused

Once research ends, however it ended, planning is paused. While it is paused nothing is implemented: Send sprint, the ribbon's Send Sprint, and the sprint's Ctrl+Shift+Enter are disabled, their tooltips saying planning is paused for review, and no proposal from the research is added to the plan by itself. Stories can still be written, edited, ordered, and moved, and proposals still accepted or rejected one by one, since those only change the plan.
Nothing of the plan starts while it is paused, not only nothing new: a story of Current sprint still waiting in the queue, not yet started, is held where it is, as a queued prompt being edited is held, as the [QueueList](../prompt-mode/queue-list/index.md#queue-list) says, its row reading "Held for review", muted, and its lane waits on it; a story already running when the pause began runs on to its end, since stopping it would leave its work half done, and the bar says how many are still running. A chain's next step, as a story's steps are sent, is held the same way. Once the pause ends, by Resume or Approve, what was held goes on in its order, as though nothing had stopped it.
The pause is plain to see: a bar across the top of Planning, in the theme's warning colour, with a pause icon, reads "Paused for review", names the research it is waiting on, with a link that opens its findings, and holds two buttons, "Resume", which ends the pause, and "Approve and send sprint", which ends it and sends Next sprint at once. The Planning tab in the body shows a small pause icon beside its name, and the ribbon's Planning tab a warning dot, while it is paused. Pressing either button is the only way the pause ends; nothing the agent does, and no time passing, ends it. A second research while paused keeps the pause, naming the latest.
The pause is saved with the plan, in `order.json`, with the research it waits on, as soon as it begins, so it is still paused, and still shown so, after the project is closed and opened again, the application restarted, or the window reloaded, until it is resumed or approved.

## Keyboard

Everything in Planning can be done from the keyboard. Tab moves through the section headings' buttons, the rows, and the open story's fields in order, and the focused one shows the theme's focus ring. In a list, Up and Down move between rows, Enter opens or closes the focused story, A accepts the focused proposal, E edits it, and R rejects it, and Alt+Up and Alt+Down move the focused story up or down, across sections as dragging does. Ctrl+N adds a story, Ctrl+Enter moves the focused story to Next sprint, or to the Backlog from it, Ctrl+Shift+Enter sends the sprint, and M opens the focused story's mode picker, whose options are picked with the arrow keys and Enter. Delete deletes the focused story after a confirmation. Escape closes what is open, a menu, a story, or the drafting or research panel, one at a time. Every button and control has a label a screen reader reads, as its visible text or, for an icon, its tooltip, and each shortcut is given in the tooltip of the control it stands for.
Ctrl+Shift+D opens Draft stories, focusing its request box, where Enter starts the draft, as Ctrl+Enter also does, and Shift+Enter adds a new line; Ctrl+Shift+R opens Research, focusing its box, where Ctrl+Enter starts it; F6 moves focus between the column's regions, the pause bar, each section, an open panel, and back, so each is a single stop; within the pause bar, Tab reaches Resume and Approve and send sprint; within an open story, Tab reaches its steps, its Add step, and its Spec citations, each citation opening on Enter; and within Findings, Enter opens the focused finding in its tab. The Start automatically switch is reached by Tab on Next sprint's heading and toggled with Space. Focus never lands on something hidden or disabled, and after an action it stays where it was or moves to what the action made, as the new story or the next proposal, never back to the top.
# Body

## How To Build

A Body should be built as a reusable component that will be reused throughout the rest of the codebase.  A component is configurable through arguments or properties that alter its behaviour, appearance, and details.  A Body should encapsulate all of its own reusable behaviour, while leaving the wiring, integration, and integration to the domain of the application.

## Theme

Drawn in the [Theme](../../ui/theme/index.md#theme): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

## Pitch

The main window's body: the area to the right of the project sidebar, where the tasks sent to the harness, and the files opened in tabs beside them, are shown, and the chat input they are sent from.

## Description

Beneath the [Ribbon](../../ui/components/ribbon/index.md#ribbon), to the right of the [LeftSidebar](../../ui/components/left-sidebar/index.md#left-sidebar), which runs the full height beside it, and reaching the window's right edge. It is part of the [PromptEditor](../prompt-mode/index.md#prompt-editor).
The [ChatInput](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input) lives within the body, along its bottom: its left edge against the project sidebar, and above it, beneath the body's tab bar, the selected tab's contents: the message list, or an open file. While a task runs, the [RightSidebar](../../ui/components/right-sidebar/index.md#right-sidebar) runs the body's full height at its right, beside the tab bar, the selected tab's contents, and the chat input, and the chat input's right edge is against it: the chat input never runs beneath the right sidebar. While that sidebar isn't there, the chat input reaches the window's right edge.
The body is flat and quiet: the selected tab's contents, the message list or an open file, sit on the theme's base surface, #444444 in dark mode, running edge to edge with no border, and the chat input along the bottom is set apart from them only by its own darker tab strip, as the [ChatInput](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input) says, with no line between them.

## Sliding

Whenever something slides out or back along one of the body's edges, as the [RightSidebar](../../ui/components/right-sidebar/index.md#right-sidebar) does, everything else in the body moves smoothly with it, frame by frame, rather than jumping once the slide is over: the tab bar, the selected tab's contents, the Ask conversation while it shows, and the chat input all keep their right edge against the sliding edge throughout, so they narrow or widen together, in step with it and with each other. None of them lags behind another, is left at its old width until the slide settles, or runs beneath what is sliding. Their contents are laid out anew at each width as it changes, text wrapping and rows reflowing as they go: the tab bar's tabs, the chat input's text and buttons, the message list's table, and an open file's editor. A slide that reverses partway moves them back from wherever it had reached.

## Contents

Everything that can be in the body:

- a tab bar along its top, holding a Chat tab, a tab for each file open, and the Planning tab while it is open
- the [Planning](../planning/index.md#planning), beneath the tab bar while its tab is selected
- the [MessageList](../prompt-mode/message-list/index.md#message-list), the chat history, shown beneath the tab bar while the Chat tab is selected
- the hint shown in the message list's place before any task has been sent, or while no project is open, as the [PromptEditor](../prompt-mode/index.md#prompt-editor) and the [NoProjectState](../no-project/index.md#no-project-state) say
- an [Editor](../editor/index.md#editor) for each open file, shown beneath the tab bar while its tab is selected
- a task view for each task opened in a tab of its own, as its task tabs say, shown beneath the tab bar while its tab is selected
- the [AskConversation](../prompt-mode/ask-conversation/index.md#ask-conversation), in the Chat tab's place beneath the tab bar, while the chat input's Ask tab is selected
- the [ChatInput](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input), along the bottom beneath whichever tab is selected, and beneath the Ask conversation too
- the [RightSidebar](../../ui/components/right-sidebar/index.md#right-sidebar), at the right of all of these, the tab bar and the chat input included, while a task runs or is queued, or it is opened by hand

An [InsetPanel](../../ui/components/inset-panel/index.md#inset-panel) floats over the whole window, the body included, but is never part of it.

## Ask Mode

While the chat input's Ask tab is selected, the Ask conversation, as the [AskConversation](../prompt-mode/ask-conversation/index.md#ask-conversation) says, takes the Chat tab's place in the body, filling all of it beneath the tab bar and above the chat input, as the message list fills it for every other mode: the body never splits, and nothing is shown beside the conversation. The Chat tab then reads "Ask" in Ask's colour. Selecting another mode's tab brings the message list back in its place, as it was left, and selecting Ask again brings the conversation back, scrolled where it was; the switch is at once, with nothing sliding. A file or task tab selected shows that file or task whatever mode is selected, and selecting Ask while one is shown selects the Chat tab, so the conversation is in view.

## Tabs

Along the top of the body runs a tab bar, in gpui-kit's default tab styling, across the width the message list takes: from the project sidebar to the right sidebar while a task runs, and to the window's right edge otherwise. Its first tab, Chat, shows the message list, and is always there: it can't be closed or moved. After it comes a tab for each open file and each task opened in a tab of its own, files and tasks together, in the order they were opened unless they have been dragged since, scrolling sideways once there are more than fit.
Just one tab's contents show at a time, filling the space between the tab bar and the chat input. The chat input stays along the bottom whichever tab is selected, so a prompt can be written while a file shows. The body starts with Chat selected, and clicking a tab selects it.
Every tab in the bar, Chat and each file's alike, is laid out the same plain way, with nothing extra around it: the bar's full height, 32 pixels, its contents centred up and down in it, 12 pixels of padding at its left, and 12 at its right, and no margin of its own above, below, or beside it, so one tab ends where the next begins, with only the tab styling's own line between them. Nothing is inset from the bar's top or bottom, and the first tab starts at the bar's left edge.
A file's tab shows the file's name, then, while it has unsaved changes, a dot, and then a small close button, an icon button 16 pixels square, set close beside the name, 4 pixels from it or from the dot, with no more room between them however long or short the name is. Since the button has room of its own around its icon, a file tab's right padding is 6 pixels rather than 12, so the icon sits as far from the tab's right edge as the name does from its left; the tab is only as wide as its padding, name, dot, and close button need. Chat's spinner, while something runs, sits 6 pixels after its label, inside the same padding. Hovering a file's tab shows the file's path in the project as its tooltip.
A file's tab can be dragged along the tab bar to reorder the files, as the [DragReorderBehaviour](../../ui/behaviours/drag-reorder/index.md#drag-reorder-behaviour) says, a vertical line showing the gap between two tabs it will land in, and the tab dragged following the pointer as the file's name. Chat stays first: no gap before a file's first tab, between Chat and it, shows the indicator, and Chat itself can't be dragged. Dragging a tab selects it, as clicking it does, and the selection follows the tab to its new place; nothing else about its editor changes. A press on a tab's close button closes it rather than starting a drag. A file opened afterwards still gets its new tab just after the one selected.

## Task Tabs

The Chat tab shows only the task the harness is working on now, and those running beside it, as the [MessageList](../prompt-mode/message-list/index.md#message-list)'s header shows them, or, while none runs, the task that finished last, until the next is sent. It never shows any other task: a task opened from the right sidebar's Tasks tab, as the [TasksTab](../../ui/components/right-sidebar/tasks/index.md#tasks-tab) says, or from anywhere else that opens a task, opens in a tab of its own in the body's tab bar, as a file does: a task not open yet gets a new tab just after the one selected, and is selected; opening one that already has a tab selects that tab; and opening the task Chat is showing selects Chat instead.
A task's tab is laid out as a file's is: a bar 2 pixels wide down its left in its mode's colour, its status, a spinner while it is under way, a tick, cross, or dash once it has ended, then its name, the first line of its prompt cut off with an ellipsis at 24 characters, then its close button. Hovering it shows its prompt's first lines and its mode as its tooltip. It can be dragged among the files' tabs, and closed as they are, closing it changing nothing about the task.
Beneath it, the task shows as it would at the head of the Chat tab, on its own: its header, with its status, time, compiled prompt, and buttons, then its output table, then the files it changed, scrolled to its top the first time it is shown, and as it was left after. A task still running shows its output as it comes, its table locked to the bottom while scrolled there, as the latest task's is, and carries on in its tab whether or not the tab is selected. Its tab stays open once it finishes. Opening a task in a tab doesn't select it in the Chat tab or change what Chat shows, and Chat's running tasks are never opened in tabs of their own unless asked for, a running task opened from the Tasks tab selecting it in Chat's header instead. Each open project keeps its own task tabs, as its file tabs are kept, and none is reopened when the project is opened again.

## Open File

A file opened, from the [FileTree](../../ui/components/file-tree/index.md#file-tree) or anywhere else the [OpenFile](../open-file/index.md#open-file) says, shows in an [Editor](../editor/index.md#editor) in a tab of its own, as many files open at once as are opened. A file not open yet gets a new tab, just after the one selected, and is selected. Opening a file that already has a tab selects that tab instead, leaving its editor as it was, unsaved changes and all.
Nothing slides: a file's tab is selected, and its editor shows, at once, and closing it takes it away at once too. Files never split the body among themselves; the file takes the tab bar's full width above the chat input.
Closing a file's tab, with its close button or the editor's, closes the file, the editor first asking to discard any unsaved changes. Closing the selected tab selects the tab to its right, or, with none to its right, the one to its left, which is Chat once no file is left. Closing a tab that isn't selected leaves the selection as it is.

export ui-component Planning:
    pitch:
        A plain, quick list of the work still to do, as Linear keeps issues:
        stories written ahead of time, each saying how it will be sent, Code,
        Chain, Spec, Ask, or Freeform, gathered into the next sprint and sent
        to the agent in order, all at once.

    description:
        Planning opens in a tab of its own in the body, "Planning", with a
        checklist icon, as a file opens, as the @{Body} says, from the
        ribbon's Planning tab or the palette's "Planning". It is one column
        of stories, at most 760 pixels wide, centred, in sections, each
        headed by its name and count: "Current sprint", at the top, only
        while a sprint is under way, then "Next sprint", and "Backlog"
        beneath them. A section with nothing in it reads, muted,
        "Nothing planned" or "Backlog is empty".

    stories:
        A story is one piece of work, written as it will be sent: a title,
        a prompt, and how it will be sent. Each is a row, 36 pixels tall: a
        drag grip at its left; a small mode picker, a pill reading its mode,
        "Code", "Chain", "Spec", "Ask", or "Freeform", in that mode's colour,
        as the @{PromptModes} colours it; its title, in the body's text
        colour, cut off with an ellipsis; then, at its right, muted, a small

    drafting:
----
    research:
        The agent can be asked to research a topic before anything is
        planned or built: "Research", a button beside "Draft stories" on the
        Backlog's heading, and "Research" in an open story's menu, open a
        box labelled "What should be looked into?". Research runs as a
        read-only investigation, a Question run, as the @{Sandbox} says, which
        can read the project and the web and change nothing, given the
        research prompt of the @{BakedSystemPrompts}, which asks for findings,
        not changes: what was found, where, with links to the files and
        lines it read, what it is unsure of, and what it would suggest, and
        it may end with proposals, as the proposals say. Its run is shown in
        the drafting panel as drafting's is, its live line of what it is
        reading, a Stop button, and its spinner.

        rendered as markdown with its links clickable, shown in a Findings
        list beneath the Backlog, newest first, each a row with its topic,
        when it ran, and its state, and opening in a body tab of its own to
        read whole. Findings started from a story are also listed in that
        story, beneath its steps. They are saved with the plan, in

        read again later, and can be deleted from their row's menu.

        from the research is added to the plan by itself. Stories can still

        or rejected one by one, since those only change the plan.

        way. Once the pause ends, by Resume or Approve, what was held goes

        "Approve and send sprint", which ends it and sends Next sprint at
        once. The Planning tab in the body shows a small pause icon beside
        its name, and the ribbon's Planning tab a warning dot, while it is
        paused. Pressing either button is the only way the pause ends;
        nothing the agent does, and no time passing, ends it. A second
        research while paused keeps the pause, naming the latest.

        it waits on, as soon as it begins, so it is still paused, and still
        shown so, after the project is closed and opened again, the
        application restarted, or the window reloaded, until it is resumed
        or approved.

content.text:
I've rewritten the Planning spec so it describes a kanban board. `piton check` and `piton build` both pass with no problems. All the edits are in `spec/scope/planning/index.pi`, which now imports Scrollbar.

`git status` also lists changes to Body, the ribbon's Planning tab, chat input, sandbox and a few other spec files. I didn't touch those, and `spec/scope/planning` itself doesn't show in git status at all, so it's worth checking where those changes came from.

**What changed in the spec**
- **Board:** Planning now fills the body beneath the tab bar. Its columns sit left to right in this order: Backlog, Next sprint, Current sprint, Done, then Findings last. Every column is always there, and Current sprint and Done no longer appear, disappear or collapse.
- **Sizes I chose, since the prompt gave none:** columns are 320 pixels wide and 16 pixels apart, the board has 24 pixels of padding, and cards are 8 pixels apart.
- **Columns:** each has a 32 pixel heading with its name, count and labelled actions. Actions that don't fit wrap onto a second line instead of being cut off. Each column scrolls on its own with its heading fixed at the top, and the board scrolls sideways when it's wider than the tab. Both use the Scrollbar.
- **Story card:** a new fourth part beside the row, panel and card. Its top line has the grip, the mode pill, and the status and time at the right (plus the menu button on hover). The title wraps to two lines before it's cut off, and the step count and attachment icon sit beneath it, muted. In Current sprint a card lists its steps, each with its own status, and Done cards are muted. Rows are now used only for steps in an open story and for findings.
- **Empty states:** I added two new ones: "No sprint under way. Send sprint to start one." for Current sprint and "Nothing done yet." for Done. While the plan loads, each column shows skeleton cards.
- **Pause bar:** it runs across the top of the whole board.
- **Keyboard:** I added Left and Right to move between columns. Wording about rows elsewhere now says cards.

Sending, closing, auto start and saving to `order.json` are unchanged.

**Anchors the code should follow:** `Planning.description`, `Planning.layout`, `Planning.parts`, `Planning.stories`, `Planning.sprint`, `Planning.steps`, `Planning.states`, `Planning.research`, `Planning.paused` and `Planning.keyboard`, all in `.claude/reference/scope/planning/index.md`, plus `Scrollbar`.
